# Shared provider read engine

This bundle reuses Butchr's native Jira work/idea/project, Confluence, GitHub issue/PR, Zendesk and Trello read clients. The normal server build uses the checked-in bundle, not a sibling checkout. `scripts/sync-provider-engine.ts` is a developer-only update command; `SOURCE.json` records its exact Butchr inputs.

`bun run build:providers` builds the fixed Node subprocess entry and notices. `bun run verify:providers` rejects stale source, lockfile, build scripts or generated bytes. Ship `read-process.js`, its SHA256 file, both source manifests, protocol files and third-party notices together with the server sources. The runtime verifies the fixed entry checksum before starting it.

Provider execution requires a trusted Node >=20 executable. The default is `/usr/bin/node`; the operator can choose a trusted absolute path with `BUTCHR_PROVIDER_NODE`. No executable, module or argument is selected by a client request. An unavailable runtime reports failed reads/probes; it does not start a different engine or fall back to a local account.

Each fixed child receives its job through bounded stdin. Parent capacity is two children globally and one per authorization. A 30-second deadline, cancellation and shutdown kill/reap children before capacity returns. V8 heap, response bytes, aggregate bytes and stdout are bounded. The sampled Linux RSS watchdog is best-effort, not a hard kernel memory limit. Deployment must account for parent, stream buffers and concurrent children.

Instances register bounded read subscriptions using their existing authenticated deployment/session identity. Results travel only in capability-negotiated SSE snapshots and RFC6902 updates. Owned semantic stages request fresh versions; the subscription receipt supplies the minimum version, and the client preserves each request's causal observation across retries. Sending an SSE frame is never a worker notification acknowledgment. Butchr's existing factories, event decisions, linked watcher baselines, admission and actual delivery acknowledgments remain client-owned.

Profile credentials are separate from machine keys and owner login. Owner APIs require the existing session/CSRF protections, return redacted metadata, and store credentials only in private versioned files (memory-only in fixtures). Resource contents and private links can be delivered to matching authorized instances; do not treat this as metadata-only telemetry. Filesystem reads stay local. Public webpage reads pin validated public DNS addresses, preserve TLS hostname verification and bound time/body/redirects.

Local provider switches and Trello/Zendesk risk holds still apply. Remote disconnection or master-off never selects another local account. A cold unverified bootstrap remains conservative until a verified restart. Atlassian remote staffing currently requires the same tenant as local tool/write connections; missing or mismatched tenants fail closed. No remote write proxy or worker execution lives on Servr.
